BACKGROUND

A little background

JEONGMILLA told Yonhap that she moved to Cheongpa-dong in autumn 2019, where she could see Seoul Station from her window. Walks through the surrounding neighbourhoods helped shape CheongPa Sonata, her third studio album.

INSIDE THE LYRICS

The station stays as life changes

  • Family
  • Changing plans
  • Everyday places

The song begins with a mother’s practical worries about a late journey home after a performance. The speaker answers with a small reassurance: since moving, she can walk home from the station. That ordinary detail gives the conversation its closeness; there is no grand announcement, just news that might ease a parent’s concern.

Seoul Station then connects the present to an earlier arrival for a university entrance exam. The speaker once expected to become a painter and now makes a living singing. She acknowledges how often life has changed since she was twenty without deciding whether those changes amount to success or failure.

The station also offers routes to her hometown and a school friend’s house. It belongs to her relationships as much as her memories. The closing wish to take a train to the sea before summer keeps the future modest and open: another possible departure from a familiar place.

ABOUT THE ARTIST / 정밀아

JEONGMILLA

JEONGMILLA is a folk singer-songwriter who writes about her life by paying attention to the places around her. On CheongPa Sonata, that means the streets, neighbours and public squares within walking distance of home.

She released her first two studio albums in 2014 and 2017, followed by her third, CheongPa Sonata, in 2020. She studied art at university and continues to make visual art alongside music.
